records.Concise description: A pioneering desktop Bitcoin wallet known for early cold-storage and multisig-oriented security workflows, now primarily a legacy project.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Armory was an influential early desktop wallet that emphasized offline signing, deterministic backups, multi-wallet management and security-conscious interaction with Bitcoin Core. The original company ceased development and maintenance passed to community maintainer goatpig. The latest verified public release located in this research is 0.96.5 from December 2018; no credible 2026 active product operation was verified.
records.Launch / history: Armory emerged around 2011–2012 and became a major early cold-storage wallet. Armory Technologies later discontinued development; community maintenance continued for a period, with the last verified release in December 2018.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Armory helped establish practical offline signing and high-security desktop wallet patterns before modern PSBT/hardware-wallet ecosystems matured.
Important technical or cultural characte: Legacy project with no verified current release activity
records.Verification basis: Legacy first-party site and community repository verify product history; absence of recent releases plus the discontinued-company notice supports HISTORICAL rather than ACTIVE.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not recommend Armory as a current default wallet without a fresh compatibility/security assessment.
Current compatibility with modern Bitcoin Core versions and operating systems is not sufficiently verified for public guidance.

records.Concise description: A self-custody Bitcoin wallet spanning BTC, Ordinals, Runes, BRC-20 and Stacks-connected assets across browser and mobile clients.
records.Deeper researched summary: Xverse is a Bitcoin-focused self-custody wallet developed by Secret Key Labs. It separates ordinary BTC handling from Taproot-oriented asset addresses to reduce accidental inscription/token spends, and provides integrated support for Ordinals inscriptions, Runes and BRC-20 alongside Stacks-related assets. Current 2026 releases also support hardware signing with Ledger and Keystone for Bitcoin asset workflows.
records.Launch / history: Xverse launched in the early 2020s and expanded substantially during the 2023 Ordinals era; hardware and asset support continued to broaden through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Xverse is one of the clearest bridges between ordinary Bitcoin wallet use and the Ordinals/Runes application ecosystem, making it a required canonical Wallets entity rather than merely an Ordinals accessory.
Important technical or cultural characte: Self-custody; keys encrypted on the user's device
Browser extension plus iOS and Android
Open-source components with published security material
BTC plus Ordinals, Runes and BRC-20
Separate Bitcoin and Taproot asset address handling
Ledger integration; current browser support also includes Keystone
Hardware-backed signing support for Bitcoin-native assets
records.Verification basis: Current 2026 Xverse first-party security, product and hardware-wallet documentation verifies custody model, asset support and current operation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not reduce Xverse to an 'Ordinals wallet'; its canonical role spans BTC and multiple Bitcoin application layers.
BRC-20 and Runes balances/validity depend on their respective protocol/indexing rules, not Bitcoin consensus alone.

records.Concise description: An open-source non-custodial Bitcoin wallet focused on BTC and Bitcoin-native asset protocols including Ordinals, BRC-20 and Runes.
records.Deeper researched summary: UniSat Wallet began as a browser-extension wallet closely associated with BRC-20 and Ordinals tooling and has expanded to mobile platforms and broader Bitcoin-native asset support. Current materials describe non-custodial key control and support for multiple Bitcoin address types, UTXO management, Ordinals, BRC-20, Runes and newer application protocols such as Alkanes.
records.Launch / history: UniSat emerged in 2023 alongside the early BRC-20 ecosystem and remains actively developed through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: UniSat is a major Bitcoin application wallet and infrastructure participant for inscription/token ecosystems, with direct relevance to Ordinals, Runes and marketplaces.
Important technical or cultural characte: Browser extension plus iOS and Android
Legacy, nested SegWit, native SegWit and Taproot address support
records.Verification basis: Current first-party site, documentation and open-source extension repository verify lifecycle, custody model, supported platforms and Bitcoin-asset scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Token/protocol support is application-layer and indexer-dependent where the protocol itself is not Bitcoin consensus state.
Do not treat UniSat marketplace functions as a reason to duplicate the entity in MARKETPLACES.

records.Entity / project type: browser / mobile Bitcoin and Stacks wallet
records.Concise description: A self-custody Bitcoin and Stacks wallet, evolved from Hiro Wallet, with current browser and mobile clients and safeguards for Bitcoin collectibles.
records.Deeper researched summary: Leather provides a browser extension and mobile apps for BTC, Stacks-linked assets, inscriptions/collectibles and related application interactions. It is open-source and integrates Ledger. Leather previously supported Runes directly but ended in-wallet Runes management on April 16, 2026; the underlying keys/addresses remain user-controlled, so the change is a product-support change rather than a loss of asset ownership.
records.Launch / history: The Hiro Wallet product was rebranded as Leather in 2023. Native mobile clients arrived later, and direct Runes support was discontinued April 16, 2026 while broader Bitcoin/Stacks development continued.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Leather is a significant Bitcoin application wallet because it connects base-layer BTC and collectibles with the Stacks ecosystem while demonstrating how wallet-level support can change even when user-controlled assets remain on-chain.
Important technical or cultural characte: Browser extension plus iOS and Android
records.Verification basis: Current Leather site and April 2026 first-party Runes deprecation notice verify current platform/support state.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not list Runes as a current managed asset in Leather after April 16, 2026.
Runes remaining at a user's address are not erased by Leather ending UI support; users must use compatible external tooling to manage them.
The Wallets profile should remain Bitcoin-focused even though Leather spans Stacks.
